analysis.one_liner: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance (Murugappa Group) is a diversified NBFC that lends against vehicles, homes/property and small businesses, and also runs a general insurance joint venture.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results are due at a board meeting on 2026-10-28, about ten days from now. The last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026) showed standalone PAT up 46% YoY to roughly ₹1,656 crore on AUM growth of 23% to about ₹2,54,392 crore, but the stock has fallen 18.8% from its August 2026 peak and sharply underperformed both Nifty and peer Bajaj Finance over the last three months.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a lending business, not a product company - it borrows money and re-lends it against vehicles, homes and small-business collateral, earning the spread. The core lending book is growing fast and profitably, but the market has still marked the stock down hard in the last quarter. That tension - strong reported numbers versus a falling share price - is the thing to watch; it suggests either the market is pricing in asset-quality or funding-cost worries not yet visible in the headline profit, or NBFC stocks broadly have been re-rated lower.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) standalone: AUM ₹2,54,392 cr (+23% YoY), disbursements ₹29,612 cr (+22%), standalone PAT ₹1,656 cr (+46% YoY), NIM up to 8.2% from 7.8%, net credit cost improved to 1.5% from 1.8%. GNPA rose to 4.50% from 4.29% YoY, NNPA 2.95%. A separate 'Gross Stage 3' figure of 3.29% also appears in some sources on what looks like a different basis - this could not be reconciled with the 4.50% GNPA figure, so treat the exact asset-quality number with some caution. Total income figures also vary slightly (~₹8,933-8,957 cr) depending on whether standalone or consolidated basis is used - not a red flag, just a comparability note. Consolidated profit (₹1,789 cr, +42%) was held back by the general insurance JV, whose profit fell 19.7% YoY as its combined ratio worsened to 120.4% from 114.8% - the core NBFC lending business is performing better than the consolidated number suggests.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock has returned 165% versus 25% for Nifty and 28% for peer Bajaj Finance - a genuinely strong long-run run, and these figures are already split-adjusted for the 5:1 split in June 2019, so the comparison is clean. But the recent picture is weaker: over 1 year the stock is down 5.5% (still less bad than Nifty's -9.5% or peer's -7.3%), while over 3 months it has fallen 12.7% against Nifty's -4.9% and peer's -7.0%, and sits 18.8% below its August 2026 peak. This drawdown is not explained by any corporate action - it is a genuine price decline that has outpaced the broader market and the peer.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of about 23.4x and P/B of about 4.4x on an ROE near 19.4%, this is not a cheap stock in absolute terms. Why it isn't cheap: a long record of 20%+ AUM growth and the Murugappa Group pedigree have historically earned it a premium multiple versus plain-vanilla NBFCs. Whether it is cheap is a separate question - the recent 18.8% correction has brought the multiple down from its August highs, but there's no verified historical average P/B here to say whether today's 4.4x is low, fair or still rich by this company's own standards.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here looks both volume- and margin-led, which is the healthier combination: AUM grew 23% and disbursements 22% (volume), while NIM also expanded 40 bps to 8.2% and credit costs improved (margin/quality). Growth is broad-based across segments - vehicle finance (+19% AUM), housing/LAP (+23%) and the smaller small-business loan book SBPL (+40%, off a smaller base so the percentage should be read in that light) - rather than concentrated in one product.
analysis.health_read: Credit costs actually improved YoY (1.5% vs 1.8%), which is a good sign that provisioning discipline is holding even as GNPA ticked up to 4.50% from 4.29%. The real risk to watch is less about whether profits convert to cash - this is a lending business where leverage, not cash conversion, is the core risk metric - and more about financial risk: debt-to-equity is roughly 6.9x, which is structurally high but typical for this business model, making it sensitive to funding-cost or liquidity shocks rather than to a sudden collapse in the lending business itself. Business risk is present too, visible in the slight NPA uptick and the weaker insurance JV, but it looks more like a modest asset-quality drift than a crisis so far.
analysis.ownership_read: The Murugappa Group holds the company via Cholamandalam Financial Holdings, with promoter holding at roughly 49.2% as of June 2026, down gradually from about 49.9% a year earlier through open-market sales - a trend worth watching rather than a one-off. No share pledging was found or reported. Institutional ownership is split roughly 24.5% FII and 20.6% DII, with mutual fund holdings rising modestly; no individually named marquee investor (the kind often highlighted in market commentary) was found on the register, so none should be assumed.
strengths: AUM grew 23% YoY to ~₹2,54,392 crore with disbursements up 22% to ~₹29,612 crore in Q1 FY27
NIM expanded to 8.2% from 7.8% while net credit cost improved to 1.5% from 1.8% YoY - growth and discipline moving together
Standalone PAT grew 46% YoY to ~₹1,656 crore in Q1 FY27, off an already-sizeable ₹1,138 crore base, not a low-base illusion
Diversified, actively-tapped funding base through the year (multiple NCD, subordinated and perpetual bond raises), aided by RBI's reversal of the extra risk-weight on bank lending to NBFCs
watchpoints: GNPA rose to 4.50% from 4.29% YoY and NNPA stands at 2.95% - a mild but real deterioration to track in the Oct 28 results
Stock down 18.8% from its August 2026 peak and sharply underperforming Nifty and peer Bajaj Finance over the last 3 months, with no corporate action to explain it away
General insurance JV profit fell 19.7% YoY as its combined ratio worsened to 120.4% from 114.8%, dragging consolidated numbers below the core lending business's performance
Promoter holding has drifted down from ~49.9% to ~49.2% over the past year via open-market sales, and leverage (debt/equity ~6.9x) remains structurally high
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results on 2026-10-28 - specifically whether GNPA/NNPA keep rising or stabilise, and whether the NIM/credit-cost improvement seen in Q1 continues - will show whether the recent stock weakness is the market front-running a real asset-quality shift or an overreaction to a strong underlying quarter.
